utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have something extra here in case you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The Chamber will issue a decision on the admission of 65 ter 25082, a five-page excerpt from the expert report entitled "Inconsistencies of experts Berko Zecevic and Richard Higgs in cases of the shelling of Sarajevo," which Witness Subotic coauthored with another Defence expert, Witness Mile Poparic. The Prosecution used the first and the third pages of this document during its cross-examination of Subotic on the 16th of May, 2013, and sought its admission on the same day. By way of background, the Chamber recalls that in its "Decision on Prosecution's request to exclude portions of reports of Mile Poparic" issued on the 12th of March, 2013, it granted, inter alia, the Prosecution's request to redact certain sections of that expert report, including section A2 that contains these five pages. Requesting the admission of 65 ter 25082, the Prosecution submits that this document identifies some areas where the Prosecution and the Defence "have common grounds" and that it also shows "pictures about multiple-barrel rocket launchers." The accused's legal advisor responds that he has no objection to the admission but wishes to have the option of tendering additional pages from the redacted section of the expert report as there might be other relevant material therein. The Chamber notes that when granting the Prosecution's request for exclusion of section A2 in its decision of the 13th of March, 2013, it considered that this section contains Poparic's analysis of a report coauthored by Zecevic which is not part of the trial record and "thus there is no evidentiary basis against which to assess the analysis" in that section. Accordingly, the Chamber found that "the analysis of a non-admitted report of Zecevic discussing unscheduled incidents would not assist it in its determination of Zecevic's credibility as an expert." In this light, the Chamber considers that there is no basis to admit 65 ter 25082 for the purpose of challenging Subotic's finding for the same reason that the Chamber excluded section A2. The Chamber would also not be assisted in its determination of Subotic's credibility as an expert since it decided not to admit these portions of her coauthored report. Accordingly, the Chamber denies the admission of 65 ter 25082. The next matter is related to a subpoena. The Chamber is seized of the request to the Trial Chamber to suspend the subpoena to allow Tolimir to file an appeal against the decision on the accused's motion to subpoena Zdravko Tolimir and -- against the subpoena. In this regard, the Chamber wishes to hear from the parties, in particular as to witnesses standing to challenge this subpoena. While the Chamber notes the Rules provide that only parties can appeal the decisions, it also is cognisant of the Jonathan Randal decision in which the Trial Chamber that issued the subpoena against the witness, Jonathan Randal, who was a war correspondent of Washington Post, if my memory's correct, granted the leave to appeal the decision, and the Appeals Chamber set aside the subpoena on several reasons. So whether -- I'm wondering whether the Chamber could hear the views of the Prosecution and the Defence, if it so wishes, by the end of this week. Well, that said, we'll bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would the witness take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kosoric. Please be seated and make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you commence your evidence, Mr. Kosoric, I must draw your attention to a certain Rule that we have here at the International Tribunal, that is Rule 90(E). Under this Rule, you may object to answering any question from the accused, Mr. Karadzic, the Prosecution, or even from the Judges if you believe that your answer will incriminate you in a criminal offence. In this context, "incriminate" means saying something that might amount to an admission of guilt for a criminal offence or saying something that might provide evidence that you might have committed a criminal offence. However, should you think that an answer might incriminate you, as a consequence you refuse to answer the question, I must let you know that the Tribunal has the power to compel you to answer the question, but in that situation, the Tribunal would ensure that your testimony compelled in such circumstances would not be used in any case that might be laid against you for any offence save and except the offence of giving false testimony. Do you understand what I have just told you, Mr. Kosoric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Excellencies. Good morning to everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before we start I have to ask you and I have to remind myself at the same time that we have to speak slowly and that we should make ample pause between my questions and your answers in order to have everything recorded properly. Lieutenant-Colonel, did you provide a statement to my Defence team?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up 1D07051 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that statement on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you read and sign the statement?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Longer breaks, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the second page with his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does the statement truthfully reflect all those things that you said or should some things be changed in the statement?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No, nothing needs to be changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I were to put the same questions to you today in this courtroom, would your answers be the same?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: They would be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, I'm tendering this statement into evidence pursuant to Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3562, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I'm going to read a short summary of the statement in English. [In English] In July 1995, Svetozar Kosoric was assistant Chief of Staff for intelligence of the Drina Corps of the VRS and held the rank of Lieutenant-Colonel. During the Prosecution case, Momir Nikolic testified that on the morning of 12th of July, 1995, just prior to the last meeting with the Dutch Battalion and the -- at the Hotel Fontana, he had a conversation with Lieutenant-Colonel Vujadin Popovic and Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric outside of the hotel. During this conversation, according to Momir Nikolic, Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic informed him that the Muslim men from Srebrenica were to be transported to Bratunac and killed and that Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric confirmed this instruction. Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric states that those claims by Momir Nikolic are completely false. Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic never said anything like that in his presence, and Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric never said anything like that himself. Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric had no information or instructions that the Muslims from Srebrenica were to be killed. He was not aware of any plan to kill Muslims from Srebrenica. And that's the summary, and at that moment I do not have other questions for Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Kosoric, as you have noted, your evidence in chief in this case has been admitted in its entirety in writing, that is through your written witness statement, and now you'll be cross-examined by the representative of the Office of the Prosecutor. You understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sir, you've testified before in this Tribunal; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me try again. You've testified before in this Tribunal; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You testified as a Defence witness for Vujadin Popovic in his trial.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: At that time, you took the oath and you said that you would tell the truth just as you did today; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you stand by your testimony in that case, don't you? You did tell the truth last time you were here, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And you told the truth no matter who was questioning you, the Defence lawyers, the Prosecution, or the Judges; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When you were in the Drina Corps, your nickname was Cica; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And it's not in your statement, but if I'm correct, basically before your retirement in 2000, you were a life-long military -- career in the military, life-long military officer.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to July 1995. You were at all three Hotel Fontana meetings; correct? Two on the 11th, one on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let's talk about the 12th, the third meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have 65 -- excuse me, P4202, at page 63.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I want to show you a still picture from the trial video you've seen before, and to save time I'm not going to play the video, but this is a still from just before that meeting began on the 12th of July, and you see your subordinate, Momir Nikolic, there on the left with the number 1 on his chest; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you see your colleague from the Drina Corps, the chief of security, Vujadin Popovic, on the right, number 4.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And we won't play the video, but then you arrived and -- and that is the same time. I'd now like to go to the same exhibit, page 65. All right. You see yourself there at the end of the table where you were sitting. We have that on the video as well. You've got a number 5 on your chest; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you see that man with the number 3 on him, Ibro Nuhanovic, who came from the civilians at Potocari; right? You remember him being there?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: He must have been since we see him in the photo, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You don't remember that, shaking his hand?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And the gentleman from DutchBat with the number 1 on him, Colonel Boering, you remember him, don't you?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: They were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. They were there. So what we can see is on the 12th of July in the morning, the people here are Momir Nikolic, Vujadin Popovic, you, and Colonel Boering, right, all at the Fontana.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, I -- to save time I'm not going to play it, but one of the clips from this meeting that was played to you last time you were here testifying for Mr. Poparic was what General Mladic said at this meeting. I'll just read it out to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is from the video at 00:09:55 to 00:11:09 for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is Mladic speaking to the Muslim civilians who were there: "I want to help you, but I want absolute co-operation from the civilian population because your army has been defeated. There is no need for your people to get killed, your husbands, your brothers, or your neighbours. All you have to do is say what you want. As I told this gentleman last night, you can either survive or disappear. For your survival, I demand that all your armed men, even those who committed crimes, and many did, against our people, surrender their weapons to the VRS." Now, when General Mladic says that, he's plainly saying to the Muslim civilians there that their husbands, the brothers, the men, may all be killed; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Am I supposed to answer that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. You were there as intelligence officer for the corps. That's what he's telling them; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I don't remember that conversation, but I'm sure that there is a recording of his words. So if that can be heard on the recording, I suppose it's correct. In essence, this is more or less what he said, but it's very difficult for me to remember 20 years after the event what exactly he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if you'll take -- will you take my word that that's what he said on the tape so we don't have to play it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: You don't have to play the tape. I trust you. Why shouldn't I?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So then please answer my question. As intelligence chief from the corps at this meeting, what Mladic is saying is that all the men -- that the men may be killed if all the weapons aren't surrendered; right? It's not a complicated question.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: That's what was said. That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this man Ibro Nuhanovic, number 3 there in front of you, sitting there with you, Krstic, Popovic, with Momir Nikolic out front, what happened to him after the meeting, sir? What happened to him after he fell into the hands of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I can't answer that question, but I can say the following: When it comes to the representatives from Srebrenica, including the gentleman under number 1, I returned them to Zuti Most because I was the liaison officer between the Main Staff and the representatives of the United Nations. I had brought them over with an interpreter from Zuti Most to Srebrenica, to the meeting at Fontana, and then I returned them back to the base in Potocari. What happened next I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So you don't know that after you drove this man back from the meeting that he was subsequently taken into custody and murdered and his body found in a mass grave. As you sit here today, you don't know that? This is news to you from me?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I claim with a hundred per cent certainty that I didn't know that until now, until you have told me that just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Mm-hm. We'll get to it later, but -- well, let's just move on. After this meeting, you went to Potocari on 12th July, correct, along with General Mladic and Vujadin Popovic and some others?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me read out some of your testimony about what happened when you were in Potocari. This is from your prior transcript, which for the record is 65 ter 25073 at e-court page 42: "Q. Were you aware that able-bodied men were being separated from their families while you were in Potocari? "A. I am not," this is 2009, "I am not aware of such a case. "Q. Were you aware at any time on the 12th or 13th of July that able-bodied Muslim men were separated from their families in Potocari? "A. I am not aware of that." Question from page 43: "Q. Were you aware that on the 12th of July that hundreds of able-bodied Muslim men were separated from Potocari, detained in at least one small unfinished house in Potocari, and then transported to a hangar near schools in Bratunac for the night of 12 July. "A. I am not aware of that." Do you stand by that testimony? Were you telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So last time you testified here, just like you learned today that Ibro Nuhanovic -- or I told you today that Ibro Nuhanovic had been murdered, you learned during your testimony in 2009 that men had been separated in Potocari; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I didn't know that they had been separated. I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. And just to be clear, you, chief intelligence officer of the Drina Corps in Potocari on the 12th, staying at the Hotel Fontana that night, did not know that men were being separated. That's the truth. That's the truth from Kosoric; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: That's the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's the truth. Okay. Do you remember the Hotel Fontana meeting that you were present for, that in fact Mladic told the people that men would be separated -- or, rather, screened and -- for being war criminals, that the men, something different was going to happen to them?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You don't remember that. The person you saw on the screen before, we don't need to bring it up again, Colonel Boering from the DutchBat, he was shown a picture of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I bring that up. That's 65 ter 25098.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You were shown this in the Krstic trial. Now, that's you, right, in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: No, it ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, let me tell you what Colonel Boering said when he was asked if he recognised this man. He said: "Yes, I do recognise that man." I'm reading from P03969 at page 80. "Yes, I do recognise that man. He was also during the meeting there. He was busy with the transport and organisation to bring out the Muslim people to Kladanj later on." And he said on page 81 of his transcript about you: "That's the man we were talking about, Mr. Kosovic or Kosoric, or something like that, who was responsible for transferring the refugees." So part of your job assigned to you at the Hotel Fontana meeting or that you already had was transferring the civilian population out of the enclave; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I will explain to you now how it was, and this can be confirmed to you by the Dutch officer who was with me. I and the officer from the Dutch Battalion received an assignment, and this was based on the agreement of -- reached at the meeting on the 12th that the wounded and the ill -- not that we should transport them but that we should go to the area of Kladanj where the wounded and the ill were supposed to pass on their way to Kladanj. And I received an assignment from General Krstic to find somebody from his command to clear that route of any mines, and this was agreed with the Dutch Battalion. It was this major from the Dutch Battalion who went along with me. We arrived in this place called Luka. We did what we were supposed to do there. The major from the Dutch Battalion continued along with the wounded and the ill. This major and I were charged with securing this. I didn't have any other assignment. My next task was to go to the Zepa area and that's the --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop. Stop, please.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: -- enclave as you know full well --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop, please. We'll get to that. You're getting beyond the transport issue. Well, Mr. Boering's testimony again is that you were the man he understood as responsible for the transport and transfer, and you did indeed transport and transfer civilians out of the enclave; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't have anything to do with transport. Rather, before the transport took place, he and I went to this place called Luka because the route had to be cleared of mines. And as for the transport itself, who was in charge of it, that was after what we did, after what this DutchBat officer and I did. We were there, we had a cup of coffee, and secured what we were supposed to do. And it was neither this major from the Dutch Battalion nor I who had anything to do with the transport.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I tender this photo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was just wondering how it is relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, it's -- it may not be other than for the record that this is the photo which I've put to him Major Boering identified as the man called Kosovic or Kosoric who he understood as being the person in charge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6333, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And for the record, it's a still made from the trial video of 12 July.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, after that meeting ended, 12th of July, this is what Major Boering said, page 108, after he'd started to go towards Potocari: "I then drove back to Bratunac to the Hotel Fontana and I attempted to establish contact. After trying to find out some things, I ran into Major Nikolic who said that everything had been agreed upon and that I should get lost and that there was no business of mine here." And then he was asked if there were any other VRS officers with Momir Nikolic when this conversation took place at the Hotel Fontana after the meeting, and he said at page 109: "I believe that also the gentleman with the moustache responsible for transport was present there as well. "Q. Is that the one you referred to as Kosovic or Kosoric? "A. Yes, it is."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So do you remember after the meeting on 12 July being outside with Momir Nikolic when the DutchBat came back to ask some questions and was told to get lost? You were there with Momir Nikolic at the Hotel Fontana.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You weren't there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be clarified? Is that a meeting inside the hotel or outside the hotel, in front of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: He can read the transcripts and do whatever he wants on redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Perhaps he's raised that because there was some issue in interpretation. The transcript says that Mr. Nicholls asked outside, so from Mr. Nicholls perspective and my perspective there doesn't seem to be any problem --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- but since Dr. Karadzic raised it, perhaps the interpretation didn't come through correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So do you remember that you met Major Boering when he returned back to Hotel Fontana, together with Momir Nikolic? That's the crux of the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember that, and I don't think that I was there. Had I been there, I would certainly remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Right. So that means you're telling the truth again and Colonel Boering is not telling the truth and Momir Nikolic is not telling the truth but you are. Right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I think that I am the one speaking the truth, and Boering should do the same. I certainly was at no such meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, could I have -- play video-clip 4, please, Mr. Reid.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a clip of you in Potocari on 12 July after the Hotel Fontana meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, before we do that, I was just wondering if Mr. Nicholls can give me a citation for the comment that Momir Nikolic is not telling the truth. So is there a place in Momir Nikolic's transcript where he indicates that Mr. Kosoric was with him? If so, I would like to have that citation so I can take a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll look it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop. Okay. Can we go back? Sorry, I was distracted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, it's hard to get, but did you see yourself just walking by there, behind this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what were you -- we can see just on the corner here, and we are at 00:30:20.7, that you are carrying something. What are you carrying there? It looks like a binder or notebook.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I can't remember what it was that I was carrying. Can you replay that clip?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stopped at 00:30:20.3.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember now what's in your bag?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And we can see buses there, and you've already told us that after this you were part of an escort of the people leaving, being bused to Luka from the enclave. Didn't you notice when you were taking these people out of the enclave to Luka that they were women and children and perhaps old men? Didn't you notice that there weren't men being put on these buses while you were there?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, you are saying here some things that I have never stated. I'm telling you again that I had nothing to do with the buses. Before the buses, I went to a place called Luka. A major, an officer, a Dutch officer, arrived there as well. We were there waiting for the buses to come. We made sure that sappers cleared the area of mines and the officer accompanied the ill and wounded people to Kladanj, and that is the truth, and that was when we saw these people, and there were men among them. I remember clearly there were men that I gave my cigarettes to and a tin of canned meat, and that was all happening in Luka that I saw these people. And during the transport I didn't see the people because I was in my own car.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you were there with -- on the 12th with General Mladic; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. You testified to this before. When you went to Potocari on the 12th, you were there with General Mladic. That's why you went. You were part of his entourage.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I wasn't part of Mladic's entourage. All of us who were at the meeting went to Potocari after the meeting. It was a very short thing in Potocari, some five to ten minutes, and since I had a different task to attend to, I went to Kladanj right after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Well, we heard in this courtroom from Karadzic Defence witness Petar Uscumlic a couple days ago. He went, as you did, with General Mladic to Potocari on the 12th, and he testified plainly that he saw men being separated, and he said probably other people saw it too. So, now, are you seriously telling me that a civilian interpreter knew more about the separations going on in Potocari on the 12th of July when you, the Drina Corps head of intelligence -- than you, the Drina Corps head intelligence, when you were there also on the 12th of July? That's a serious assertion?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. The testimony from Mr. Uscumlic was that he spent several hours in Potocari. I don't think it's fair to put that to the witness in the way he's done it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, what Mr. Uscumlic testified to was when he was with Mladic, Mladic addressed the lake of people, which is at the beginning, which is when Mr. Kosoric would have been there, and that then they -- he looked over and saw the separations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think the question was so unfair. I will consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We see nothing wrong with the question. Could you answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I remember, I spent 10 to 15 minutes in Potocari at the most, and then I went to Kladanj to do the tasks that I was assigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So forget about you being there for 10 to 15 minutes. You spent the night of the -- you were in Bratunac. You're the intelligence officer. You still knew less than civilian -- than a civilian interpreter. That's your testimony; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. Okay. Let me read back to you part of your testimony since you just brought something up. This is from your testimony at e-court page 44. You were asked about the same clip and about seeing buses beside -- behind you, et cetera. Question -- this is about you in Potocari on the 12th of July. "Q. What are you doing there? "A. I have already said that after the meets with Mladic at the hotel and with the representatives of the Dutch battalion and the Muslims, all of us went to Potocari because Mladic wanted to address the people of Srebrenica. "Q. So what are you doing there? "A. I've already answered your question. We -- all of us went there. Mladic said that we should all go to Potocari for him to address the people of Srebrenica. I couldn't avoid it. "Q. So were you doing any intelligence work? "A. I was not. "Q. You were just part of Mladic's entourage? "A. Yes, I was. "Q. And you did nothing else? "A. Nothing." That's what you said last time you were here under oath. Were you telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, I won't push it, it's a small point, but you just said you weren't part of his entourage and last time you said you were. That may be a semantic issue. But you stand by the fact that you were doing nothing?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And that's -- that's the truth, too; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: The truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, let me move on. Our case is that men were separated in Potocari. I don't think it's in dispute since Mr. Karadzic asked yesterday of his witness, "Did you see the able-bodied men being separated," and asked him that twice. Those men, our case is, were taken prisoner, and there was quite a sizable number of them. In your role as chief of intelligence, wouldn't it have been part of your job to question and gain intelligence from these prisoners? For example, to find out about the movements of the Muslim column, to find out how many men were in the Muslim column walking through the woods, to find out how well armed they were? Wouldn't it have been part of your job to get intelligence from prisoners taken on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: That's correct what you're saying, and that was my job, but I didn't do that job. My -- what I was doing was the job of a liaison officer, and I was given other assignments, and that's why I wasn't performing that job. I didn't even take a single soldier or civilian for an interview, because I had other tasks that I was given and that I had to attend to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Were you aware that prisoners were interrogated those days?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No, because I went to do a different assignment, and that was far away, 60, 70, perhaps even 80 kilometres away. And I had no contact with Srebrenica or other organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You're talking about Zepa; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have P04388, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Take a look at this document quickly if you can read it. If you can't read it, tell me. It's from the 12th of July, 1995. It's from your colleague Vujadin Popovic, who you were in Potocari with that day. To the Main Staff, security and intel. And he states in paragraph 3: "We are separating men from 17 to 60 years of age, and we are not transporting them. We have about 70 of them so far, and the security organs and state security are working with them." Now, you just testified here that you didn't know about prisoners being interrogated. So for that to be true, we have to see from this document that the Main Staff intel and security is being told that there were prisoners and that security and state security are working with them, that the Drina Corps command is being told that, that it's being done by your counterpart in the security branch. So to the side of you and above you, people know that separated men are being interrogated, but you didn't know. You stick to that.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I do stand by that, and this is the first time I'm seeing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The Prosecution counsel is kindly requested to speak into the microphone at all times.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I will try. Thank you, interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, you keep talking about going to Zepa when I ask about what you knew, but last time you were here, you testified that to the best of your recollection you were in Bratunac on the morning of the 13th. This is at e-court pages 21 and 22 of your testimony last time. Sir, where were you on the morning of 13 July? This is the day after that Hotel Fontana meeting we spoke about that occurred on the 12th. "I'm afraid I don't remember those details, but on the 13th -- on the 13th, I went to Vlasenica to find the commander of the staff," and you go on. And then you say on page 21, "on the 13th, I did not go back" to Bratunac. "Q. And how did you travel from Bratunac to Vlasenica on the 13th? "A. On the 13th I travelled, I think, in a Golf car. "Q. And which road did you take? "A. I took the main road, Bratunac-Vlasenica. "Q. So Bratunac-Kravica-Konjevic Polje-Milici-Vlasenica. "A. That's right. "Q. At about what time did you set out from Bratunac on the 13th to do that. "A. I don't know, I really can't remember. "Q. Well, what -- don't worry about time. Morning, noon, or night? Morning, afternoon, or night? "A. I believe it was around noon, perhaps." And I'll ask you a question about that in a minute, but could I please have - this may help you remember - 65 ter 02300.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Page 11 in English, page 21 in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's a receipt from the Hotel Fontana, dated the 14th July, accommodation up to the 13th of July, and you're listed there. Now, does that help you remember -- and I don't want to make this a compound question. Do you stand by your testimony, then, especially seeing this receipt, that actually you were in Bratunac on the morning of the 13th and that's when you began your trip to Zepa?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: This is not true. I'm fully sure that on the 12th I spent the night at Vlasenica, and on the 13th I was at the Zepa command post, because from Zepa and Bratunac, units were arriving that took part in the Zepa operation. It also says here Obrad Vicic. He was at the forward command post on the 13th as well. He was Chief of Operations. And they all arrived on the 13th and reported to the commanders of those units and the staff leading this operation. I don't know how come this was drafted, but it cannot be correct. There must be more documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay, okay.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: -- from Zepa --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you this then: Why is it that in your statement now, it implies that after you went to Luka you went straight to Vlasenica on the 12th, whereas in your sworn testimony last time you remember the route you took from Bratunac on the 13th through Kravica, Konjevic Polje, and Milici? Why is your memory better now than when you testified in 2009?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Frankly speaking, I must have made a mistake, but now the image is much clearer of all this. The 13th is simply not possible. We were at Zepa on the 13th. I may have made a mistake. But on the 12th, I was with the Dutch major at Luka, and that's certain. That was in the afternoon. I spent the night at Vlasenica, and in the morning I continued to Zepa. I may have misspoken or maybe I -- the date I mentioned was wrong, because after all, it was long ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So on the afternoon of the 13th you're in Zepa. That's your sworn truthful testimony.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: With General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question? I didn't understand, or maybe I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: With General Krstic in Zepa on the afternoon of the 13th?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: On the afternoon of the 13th there was a briefing by all commanders that received units coming from Srebrenica. That must have been in the afternoon or in the early evening hours. There must be documents about that or an order, because they reported to him that they arrived, that they took their positions, and that they were awaiting further instructions. That was on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So the answer is --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So the answer to my question then is yes, you were with Krstic on the afternoon of the 13th in Zepa. That's your truthful testimony.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, it was not Zepa but Krivace --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah, the IKM.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: -- that's the exact location of the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: On the 13th in the afternoon --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 20 the witness did not say that was on the 13th, but it must have been the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: On the afternoon, late afternoon of the 13th, Krstic was in Vlasenica being promoted to corps commander. He wasn't in Zepa. Right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know where he was, but on the 13th he was at the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript, please. I even said in English it should have been rather than it must have been. That's what the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, before I move on may I tender those Hotel Fontana, the two pages?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm being told --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's Exhibit -- it will be Exhibit P6334.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'm being told that I should say that it's being uploaded, just those pages, as 65 ter 02300A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now I want to move on to the topic of the murders of the persons who were separated in Potocari on the 12th of July and the murders of the other Muslim men who were captured. And let me read again from your transcript before at page 14, speaking about the people in Potocari: "Q. Well, it's more than possible, isn't it, sir? You know what happened to the roughly 50 [sic] to 1.000 men separated outside Potocari that day," speaking of 12 July. "They were ... murdered, weren't they?" "A. I don't know, I wasn't there. Were they killed, were they not killed, I don't know." That was you telling the truth last time you testified; right? You didn't know the men separated in Potocari had been murdered.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I'm still saying that I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So you don't know today.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Well, today is something else. I got information from the media, from this Tribunal. Now I know it happened, but I didn't know then.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Right. So let's make sure it's clear. The Drina Corps intelligence chief learned about the murders that took place in the Drina Corps area of responsibility from the media.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Not only the media. Now I remember well, and I prepared for this testimony too. It may have been in September or October that other international bodies spoke to that about -- spoke about that to us. My intelligence work has a totally different subject matter. What you're talking about is within the remit of the police and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Right. So just so we know then, you didn't know till September or October about the murders, and you learned that from - how did you put it? - international bodies. Not VRS bodies, international bodies.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: There was talk about it in pubs, but those were rumours, and I didn't believe them. And apart from that, this isn't my job.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it had been recorded in the transcript what the witness said, it would have been clearer. He said, "We only started believing it then, after learning it from foreigners, from the international community." That's what he said. We can check it against the tapes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So then just to finish this, it was in September or October when you learned and believed that these murders had, in fact, taken place, that they weren't just rumours, that there'd been mass murders of Muslim prisoners?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you learned it not because of your intelligence chief role, because by that point everybody knew about it.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Not everybody. I only heard it for the first time and believed that probably those international bodies had correct information.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, how did you hear about it from the international bodies? Were you having meetings with the international bodies in your role as intelligence chief, or did you just read about these international bodies' findings?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: We mostly read this information from the media and newspapers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. And then it must have been a nasty shock to you as a senior officer in the Drina Corps that these murders had taken place in the Drina Corps area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was very much surprised, because there is no order that -- that can say -- that can tell anybody to do that. Nobody must follow such an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Hmm. Well, that brings me to another topic -- same topic, rather. When you were asked about the meeting -- or if not using the word "meeting," about the time when you were with Vujadin Popovic and Momir Nikolic in front of the Hotel Fontana. On direct examination from Popovic's lawyer you were asked, speaking about the statement by Popovic that all the Balijas would be killed: "Did you ever talk about anything like this to Momir Nikolic or did you tell him any of these things I now read back to you," which was Momir Nikolic's statement? "A. I've been listening carefully, this sort of thing is never dealt with in this way. No conversation could have occurred outside the hotel. That would have been impossible. All I know is I was ordered something to the effect that we had nothing to do with the Muslim people, the captured soldiers ... I was told that the civilian authorities in the Main Staff would be taking charge. I was told that the units involved in Srebrenica, on that day or the following day, would be off to the Zepa enclave. What this document says is inaccurate. A decision must be taken at a higher level, at a meeting. This is not the sort of decision that is taken outside some hotel." That was your testimony under oath last time about the meeting. And then you were asked about it again. "Q. Would such a decision, a serious decision like this, be made by General Mladic with his most senior staff inside a meeting room? Is that how such a decision to kill all the prisoners would be made? "A. Certainly, that is how a decision would be made, behind closed doors. Certainly not something out in the open where people could then talk about it. It was possible that such a decision was taken." Now, do you stand by that testimony?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes. I stand by it, but I've never heard anyone order anything like that, but anything is possible. So if anybody took that decision, that was the way to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. And actually it happened exactly the way Popovic said, outside the Hotel Fontana before he went down to Potocari, didn't it? Men were separated and then murdered, and he's been found guilty of genocide for taking part in those murders; right? It happened just the way he said it, and he's been convicted of it.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Well, Popovic never said that. I never heard him say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Now, Pavle Golic, Major Golic, was your subordinate in intel or your deputy; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: In the Drina Corps. As you sit here today, do you know that Vujadin Popovic and Ljubisa Beara, who are -- strike that. That both of those men, Beara and Popovic, have been convicted for their role, their direct role in taking part in the murder operation after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I know that they were -- that they got life. It was in the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have P05077, please. And it may perhaps be better to go to page 4 of the B/C/S. There we see the date of this intercept which is 16 July 1995. And if we could go to page 5 now. In the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I don't want to take the time to go through this whole intercept which the Trial Chamber's seen, but it involves a phone call, a call, from Zlatar, which is the Drina Corps, I think you'll remember, to Palma, which was the Zvornik Brigade, I think you'll probably remember, and -- sorry, the other way around, Zvornik calling Zlatar. And the duty officer in Zvornik says that Popovic is there and that he urgently needs 500 litres of D2 fuel or his work will stop. Then if we go to the second page of the English. The duty officer in Zvornik, we can see, says: "Is Major Golic there by any chance? "Yes. "Let me talk to him. "Golic. "Pop just called me to contact to you. 500 litres of D2 have to be sent to him immediately otherwise their work will stop." Now, we also have the fuel receipt showing that in fact at that time 500 litres of D2 was delivered to Popovic in Pilica. That's P04669. And I don't want to take the time, but there's an entry in the Zvornik Brigade duty officer notebook which also refers to this phone conversation. Our case is that at that time Vujadin Popovic is taking part in the murders of thousands -- over a thousand Muslim men that day at Branjevo farm and Pilica. That's what this fuel's for. That's what he's convicted of. Now, the question: Did you know that your subordinate Pavle Golic was assisting Popovic in this way on the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I've never heard this before. I was at least 30 kilometres away from Golic. I had no contact with him, with Vlasenica, or Zepa. I was at the front line. I had no idea. And he had no right to request this from Golic because Golic has nothing to do with that. Golic had to monitor the security situation in the western part. Golic was only in a position to go about his job. Our service and the security service are two totally different things.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. But these lines weren't completely strictly followed, were they, because part of intelligence is not -- part of intelligence work is not de-mining a road to Luka, and you assisted in that, and Golic here on this intercept is assisting Popovic in getting the fuel he needs to keep carrying out the murders. So the fact is -- the answer to my question then is that no, you had no clue that your subordinate was involved in this way.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I didn't have the faintest idea. I have never heard of this before.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have P04585. That's the Zvornik Brigade duty officer notebook, e-court pages 37 to 38. Page 38 -- page 38 of the English. Okay. That's not the right page. Oh, sorry, we're on page 1, I guess. Could we go to the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Could one of those pages be in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. This should be P04585, pages 37, 38, ET 2. I think we've got two versions of the duty officer notebook in here is the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll just read it out. This is an entry in the Zvornik Brigade duty officer's notebook for 14 July 1995. "Colonel Salapura called. Drago and Beara are to report to Golic." Now, Salapura in the Main Staff is head of intelligence; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So Beara there, we say, is the convicted Beara. The Drago there, we say, is Drago Nikolic, who's been convicted. Why are Beara and Drago Nikolic, who were intimately involved in the murder operation, being called by your boss to report to your subordinate? And to help you reference it, this is the day that the mass murders are carried out in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're asking. You are trying to elicit answers saying that I lied. I didn't know anything about this. I was 70 or 80 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop, stop, stop, stop. Let me make it simple. That's what I asked you is if you knew about this. I asked why they were doing it. If you say you don't know and this is -- you never knew about this --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Right. So your subordinate is involved with Beara and Nikolic, your boss is sending Beara and Nikolic to talk to your subordinate, but just like the fuel issue, you don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You know, 1995 was not the Stone Age. We have evidence that Krstic was receiving reports at Zepa. Command at the IKM need to be in contact with the subordinate units. You have Motorolas, you have wires, you have couriers. Just so I understand you, are you claiming you didn't know about the murder operation because since you were in Zepa you couldn't get any information about what was going on at the Drina Corps headquarters?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: That is correct. I didn't know a thing, because it wasn't my job what our units were doing. I was interested only in where the enemy was. I was into observation, reconnaissance, and so on. I only did fieldwork.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So I didn't ask if you were interested but whether you knew and received communications. So you received communications about movements of the enemy. You were in contact with Golic, because he would have been receiving information from interrogations of the captured prisoners. So you were or you were not in contact with Golic and others at the Drina Corps while you were at Zepa?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No. And there was no need for me to be in contact with him. He was at the corps command. That's where he received information from the subordinate units and forwarded it to the intelligence administration. You can see that in any document, what he did and what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So just so I understand your truthful testimony under oath here today, you're in some kind of bubble in Zepa where you have no idea what's going on in the Drina Corps area of responsibility even though you're chief of intelligence?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: That is correct. I didn't know anything, and I claim that with full certainty because I only collected information about the enemy. And I repeat that that was for the security organs, the police organs and other organs to do. I strictly did my job, and I can say, and there must be documents showing that, as soon as I arrived at the Drina Corps command, I separated my intelligence unit from the security unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Is it time for a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, if it is convenient, we shall take a break for half an hour and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. For my friend Peter Robinson, if he looks at T24554 [sic], 13th of February, 2012, that is a page where Momir Nikolic describes a conversation in front of the Hotel Fontana after the second meeting when Mr. Kosoric is there, amongst others, and he says that two Dutch officers came up, Rave and another, and he sent them away.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I want to move on to August, Mr. Kosoric, something you testified about last time you were here. This is at e-court page 62. And to orient yourself, this is in early August where you recalled that you were taking part in an effort to get prisoners from the RS who'd fled to Serbia back, and here is the question and answer to refresh your memory. "Q. Do you recall in the last part of July and early part of August, hundreds of Muslims from Zepa and Srebrenica fleeing across the Drina River and going over and seeking refuge in Serbia? "A. I know that after the fall of Srebrenica most of the Muslim soldiers crossed to Serbia. "Q. And we have intercepts in this case where General Krstic mentioned you and Popovic going over to Serbia to get those prisoners. Were you involved in that? "A. I was. "Q. And were you able to get the prisoners? "A. No. "Q. Why not?" The following page: "A. I don't know the answer to that question. Serbia simply did not wish to deliver them." Do you stand by that testimony?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Before I answer, I would kindly ask you to do something about the sound. I have a hearing-aid, and I can actually hear you better than the interpretation. The answer is yes. It's much better now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's make sure you're comfortable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Do you hear me well, Mr. Kosoric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear you very well, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we have a problem with the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- court reporter?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, who advises apparently that she'll need to reboot and a little bit of time is necessary for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's just wait a couple of minutes. Now it seems to have been resolved. Yes. Shall we start over again with your question, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Are you comfortable, Mr. Kosoric, with your hearing?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you well now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you just please repeat your answer. It didn't make it onto the transcript today. The part I read back from you -- read back to you from your testimony in the Popovic case, you said that you stood by the answer. The question was -- the answer was yes, you stood by what you'd said before. Could you affirm that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can, and I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like to show you P05258. This is an intercept which includes somebody from the VRS Main Staff named Stevo who, I think we'll learn when he comes as a witness, is Stevan Tomic, and Mr. Beara. And we see this is the 1st of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If we go to page 2 of the Serbian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, without going through it all, we say this is about the same process we just talked about, trying to bring Muslim prisoners back from Serbia. And at the bottom of the page in English we see Stevo saying: "We have some information they are relocating across the river, man, not swimming." And J, Jevtic, says: "Well, we are catching some and the MUP is too." And then S says, Stevo, says: "Listen, the men that you catch, hand them over alive to our men. We have nobody to exchange. Fuck it." And that's right, isn't it, that on the 1st of August, 1995, the VRS had nobody to exchange? You knew that as intel officer taking part in the process of trying to get these people back, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I knew nothing about this. I don't know who that Tomic is. I didn't have any information about the detainees. I didn't know whether there were any detainees or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So you didn't know how many prisoners had been taken after the fall of Srebrenica by the VRS and MUP. That was not something you knew as of August?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I didn't know. I didn't know then. I didn't know before or after. I don't know to this very day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Right. Even though interrogating prisoners is part of intelligence work; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: It is correct that that would have been part of my duties, but I did not interrogate prisoners. I was not in the territory of Srebrenica. I was on my own. I was on a field mission at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again, the question wasn't whether you interrogated prisoners yourself, but I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: P04972, please. This is an intercept from the same day also featuring Stevo from the Main Staff and Mr. Beara. The same day, 1st of August. If we go to page 2 of the English, please. It should be page 3 of the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And here Stevo says to Mr. Beara, it's about the same topic, talking about the prisoners in Serbia. "How can there be a decision when they're registering them?" "Beara: They're taking their names, but that doesn't matter, we can -- you know how, request that the ICRC escort them to us and that they can be exchanged here as written in the contract. We had no plans to kill them, the motherfuckers, but to exchange them." Now, as chief of intelligence for the Drina Corps during this period, can you help us understand why Beara, in trying to get prisoners back from Serbia, after we heard in the earlier intercept they had nobody to exchange, is saying, "We had no plan to kill them." Why would he be saying that on the 1st of August based on your knowledge as a professional intelligence officer?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Obviously I don't know. This is the first time I hear this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I see. Well, as a life-long military officer and intelligence chief of the Drina Corps, can you maybe put two and two together, that you learned in late August or September from international organisations about the murder of Srebrenica prisoners and in early August when Beara and you were trying to get prisoners back from Serbia, Beara said, "Well, we didn't have any plans to kill them," and there was no one to exchange? Is that why, do you think, using your background in intelligence?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I never discussed that with Beara. He could not issue me orders. I did not have to obey him. I had to obey my superior. And as for the place where the Muslims crossed, I went there with Popovic and I followed my orders in that. I never discussed that with Beara. I don't know what his intentions were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we have P05338. That's another intercept.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And it's General Krstic speaking with Popovic on the 2nd of August, so the next day from the ones we've just looked at, and he's saying that you and Kosoric -- sorry, that Popovic and you, Kosoric, are to go straight to Bajina Basta and bring him back his Turks. So this is what you were talking about when you testified before how you tried to get some Muslims from Serbia to bring back, but you couldn't get any; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Right. The authorities in Serbia would not allow anybody to go back. Those were the orders, and they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you certainly wouldn't have taken part in this effort to get a hold of Muslims and take them prisoner, would you, if you'd known that Vujadin Popovic had taken part in massacring Muslim prisoners two weeks earlier, would you?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Had I known that, I would have refused to have carried out the order. In the army there were two orders that did not have to be carried out, murder and physical damage. Everybody had the right to turn those orders down. In my documents you can find that I did not want to carry out some very simple tasks, for example, scouring the terrain. I didn't want to carry out those orders. All I did was my own job.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, you've said a couple times here how security was separate, you did your own job, et cetera, et cetera, strict delineation between the security and the intel branch. What were your relations like with Popovic personally? Were you friends with him? Did you joke around with him, or were you kind of distant professionals, or how would you describe it? Now, I'm speaking about July 1995 and the period after that.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I joined the corps on the 15th or 16th of June. That's when I met Popovic. That was the first time I saw him, 15 or 20 days before the Srebrenica operation started. I knew very few people in the corps. I knew Krstic, Golo Pajic who hailed from the same village. I didn't know anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you don't mind answering the question. What were your relations with him like? Friends, friendly, distant, what?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Our relationship was strictly professional. He had his office, his premises. I had mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to show a video-clip now. This is 65 ter 40620.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is -- you've seen this before. This is from around 22nd August. We believe it's in Borike or in Rogatica. You testified about this last time you were here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop. We're at 00:37.3.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's you; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Because of the timing could we go to 1:58, please, 1 minute, 58 seconds. That's fine, 1 minute, 57.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Zoka, where are you, man?"

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who's that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I can't see very well, but somebody mentioned the name Zoka, but he was the security and intelligence officer in the Rogatica Brigade. He was both an intelligent -- intelligence man and a security man. I believe that his name was Zoran Carkic. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Correct. Thank you. It is Zoran Carkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Where it stopped at 2:03.6, can we continue?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Zoka: I'm here, old man. "Cameraman: You're like an actor, Zvrko. "Zoka: A hundred per cent. "Kosoric: Hey, Zoka, what do you have there?"

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can we stop? I think it's better if we hear the sound, if there's a way to do that and just read the subtitles so we can get more of a sense of what's going on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I think we are hearing the interpretation through interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. If there's a way to just follow by reading and hear the sound without playing it twice, I would prefer that, so we can hear how people's voices are where there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you'd like to follow the subtitle without hearing the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I would prefer or I would suggest that your Chamber hear the voices, that Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But it's related to the transcript. Whether you like those part to be reflected in the transcript. That's the only way to -- to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I agree. I would rather --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can do both.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I would rather do both, Your Honours, if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So why don't we hear the interpretation first and then follow it again without interpretation, hearing the real sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. And may I just ask, Your Honours, I'm sorry, I would like to put in this whole clip, which is just a couple of minutes, but just because of -- a few minutes. But just because of time I didn't want to play it all. If I need to play whole thing to admit it, then -- I don't know if there's an -- if my friends don't object, we would admit the whole clip and the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How long is it? Why don't we play it just --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's three minutes but I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't have difficulty with it. Why don't we play it in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We stopped at 00:02:43.9.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's you and Vujadin Popovic; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And he's saying here: "Come on, the two moustachioed fellows, you know like this, Zoka. Come over here. The entire OB is present. The war criminals."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let's keep playing for just a short --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And there we just saw, stopping at 00:02:53.2, after saying, "The war criminals," Vujadin Popovic has his arms around you and Mr. Carkic just did the three-finger salute. So is this an example of your strictly professional relationship with Vujadin Popovic, who you weren't friends with?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: I saw this clip last time and now I can see that Popovic is drunk. You can tell by the way he speaks and by the way he behaves, and that was his style of behaviour. He always joked around.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. But were you drunk? Because you're also smiling and standing with him and were joking with him earlier.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No. I know that we met there. I was on my way from Kopaci, from the Visegrad brigade. That's where we met. This is in Rogatica indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. Again, that wasn't the question. You're being friendly here with Popovic, aren't you? This isn't a professional intel and security branch meeting; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Well, no comment is needed. You can see everything. I don't know whether I was also in that condition. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And the ironic thing is he is a war criminal, isn't he, Vujadin Popovic?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: If it was proven before the Tribunal, then he is. I have faith in this Tribunal. I trust it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, apart from the Tribunal's findings after you heard about the -- from the international organisations about the murders at the end of August, beginning of September, being in the Drina Corps at the same level of Vujadin Popovic, did you have any inkling before his trial that he was involved in these murders?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't have an inkling, and I was really surprised. Knowing him, it was impossible for this man to have done that. However, now I see that you've proven it, so it must be true, but he never showed any signs of having been capable of doing something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And having no idea that Popovic was involved in the murders until he -- until his trial, having no inkling of that, that's as true, your testimony on that, as everything else you've said and said in your Defence statement, right? It's the truth, just like everything you've said?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: May I admit this clip, tender this clip, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But for the record, why don't you ask the witness what the abbreviation OB meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you tell us what you heard -- what OB stands for, please?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: OB means good, healthy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, the abbreviation OB for security and intelligence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you hear Mr. Popovic is saying that entire OB is here, war criminals. What does OB mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Security organ. But security's one thing, and intelligence is another. I don't know what he meant. This man Zoran Carkic, he is subordinate to Popovic in terms of security and to me in terms of intelligence, so I don't know what he meant exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me -- let me just ask one more question. He said "war criminals." Were you arguably a war criminal for assisting in the forcible transfer of the entire population out of the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, could Mr. Nicholls show where it is -- where the qualification can be found of forcible transfer. He didn't hear it from this witness, nor did we see it in a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, I don't think Mr. Nicholls was based on this clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No. Our position is that the entire population was forcibly transferred out of the enclave, and you've told about your involvement in it in getting the convoy to Luka. Aren't you also a war criminal for helping transfer those people out of the enclave, forcibly transferring them?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR KOSORIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would kindly ask you, since the Prosecutor seems to be suspecting we -- we shouldn't really take too much time, too much of everybody's time. The Prosecution can, if necessary, interrogate me for days and then maybe they can come up with something. Why do you suspect me? Show me some evidence. Bring in witnesses. Show documents. I feel like I am being suspected of committing crimes. If I am, do lock me up. How -- how come you don't understand what my role was? Why don't you produce evidence showing that I knew anything. Show me an order of mine. How -- how did I participate? You keep attacking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I have time, I'd like to show one more short clip, but I know that I'm basically out of my time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is that about?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's the video-clip P04490 of Mr. Kosoric and Mr. Popovic at the 10th Sabotage Detachment celebration in Vlasenica in October 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
