utterances.text: Now, again you're continuing your criticism of the Vance-Owen Plan, and in the second paragraph in the English and in the second-to-last paragraph in that column in the B/C/S, you say that the functioning of the government in the mixed provinces is set up in such a way as to drive the Serbs away from these provinces. And then you say: "At least 40 per cent of the Serbs would be under alien rule. For example, the surrounds of Sarajevo, Birac, Posavina, the municipalities of Krupa na Uni, Novi Grad, Prijedor, and Sanski Most, where the Serbs are in the majority and where they have more than 50 per cent of the territory would be under Muslim rule." Now, you refer to a number territories as being where the Serbs are in the majority including Krupa na Uni. And before the war, Krupa na Uni, which was then called Bosanska Krupa, was about 74 per cent Muslim; right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Krupa na Uni is not the same as Bosanska Krupa. Krupa na Uni is on the right of the River Una and Bosanska Krupa is on the left bank.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gentlemen, this is correct, because on the right bank the Serbs are the majority, and on the left bank the Muslims are the majority. All of us, at least, know that. And I spoke about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. And Prijedor, another area where you say the Serbs were in the majority, before the war there were slightly --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: -- more -- all right. This is in 1993. But before the war, there were slightly more Muslims than Serbs in Prijedor; right? They were the largest ethnic group in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't have the information in front of me. However, given the number of Serbs who were killed on Mount Kozara, below Mount Kozara, and in Prijedor, I'm sure that there was a disbalance after that. And now that you have mentioned Prijedor, please bear with me while I tell you that 23.430 children were taken to Jasenovac from the Kozara region. Of course there should have been such a majority in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: So in this article, you're claiming that Prijedor should belong to the Serbs because it is now, after a dramatic demographic transformation from 1992 to 1993, it is now majority Serb; right? That's what you're saying here?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC
utterances.text: After the crimes that were committed in 1941 --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Dr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC
utterances.text: -- it was a given that Prijedor had to be in Serbian hands. And then you said something else. When you asked me what would happen with the Serbs, please do not ask me that. Look at the situation today. Look at what is happening with Serbs in Sarajevo and all will become clear to the Trial Chamber and to you, Madam Prosecutor, and you will see, without me mentioning the exact figures for Sarajevo, that what I have told you and what I said then I would readily repeat it today.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I note the time. I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6343, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll continue on Tuesday at 9.00, and, Mr. Lukic, can I advise you that -- not to -- you are not supposed to discuss with anybody else about your --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I don't think he heard you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I'd like to advise you, Dr. Lukic, not to discuss with anybody else about your testimony while you are giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of May, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.49 p.m.,
